en: The Essential Method for Recitation of the *Uṣṇīṣa* of the Golden-Wheel-Turning King Buddha.
Compiled by the Grand Master of the Household, Acting Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial,
Duke of Sū, with a Fief of Three Thousand Households, recipient of the purple robe, posthumously titled Minister of Works and posthumously honored with the title Dajian (Great Mirror).
The Ritual Procedures for All Offerings, translated by the Tripitaka Śramaṇa Amoghavajra of the Great Xingshan Monastery, who possesses Great and Vast Wisdom, under imperial decree,
as extensively explained in other sūtras.
Now, one merely practices at dawn and dusk;
because one constantly trains during four or three periods of the day without interruption,
the repetitions are omitted and the essentials are simplified.
When a practitioner wishes to perform the recitation of the various Buddha-uṣṇīṣas,
they should first bind the heart-seals (hṛdaya-mudrā) of the three families and recite their mantras to empower the three karmas.
The Heart Mudrā of the Buddha Family:
Interlace the two hands with the right over the left, keeping the palms facing inward;
extend both thumbs side by side. The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ jñānakāya. Next, form the heart-seal of the Lotus Family (*padmakula*).
This is the aforementioned seal, with the left wheel [of the hand] bent and inserted into the palm. The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ āruṇika (with the tongue curled back). Next, form the heart-mudrā of the Vajra family, which is the same as the heart-mudrā of the Buddha family previously mentioned.
Bend the right wheel-finger into the palm. The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ vajra-dhṛk. Next, form the Tathāgata-fist mudrā;
with the right hand, the light-covering [fingers] are held four finger-widths high.
Clench the fist and hold the left wheel upright.
With the right hand, form the Vajra-fist.
The mantra for grasping the left wheel-armor is as follows:
Oṃ bhrūṃ khaṃ jvala hūṃ. With a sound from the chest and throat like the bellowing of an ox, recite the mantra while empowering the five places of one’s own body with the mudrā.
With one's physical vessel purified and in accord with the Dharma,
one then consecrates the ground within the maṇḍala with the mudrā,
reciting the mantra seven times.
That place was transformed into a Vajradhātu Palace,
spontaneously adorned with various jewels like the pure land of a Buddha.
Next, form the mudrā for donning the vajra armor to protect the body.
This is the same heart-mudrā as the preceding Buddha-family [mudrā].
With both hands, extend the middle fingers straight upward, their tips touching one another.
Bend the upper joints into the shape of a sword;
each of the two canopies is attached to two rays at the back,
ensuring they do not touch one another.
Empower the five locations—the forehead, right shoulder, left shoulder, heart, and throat—with the mudrā.
Recite the mantra once for each location as follows:
*Oṃ chakara ṣṭri-praśami-taradara radara vaśmancara luśniśa rākṣa rākṣa maṃ hūṃ phaṭ svāhā*. Next, perform the mudrā for inviting the assembly of noble beings.
Interlace the two hands with palms facing upward;
join the two thumbs at their tips like the yoke of a carriage while reciting the mantra.
With two wheels, each turning two rays of light toward oneself,
one beckons them— either three or seven times—
visualizing the assembly of holy beings mounting this chariot and descending upon the site of practice.
The mantra for the invitation is as follows:
*Namaḥ saptarṣaye vikāya sarvatathāgatānām oṃ vajragīte kṣaya svāhā*. Next, perform the Buddha-uṣṇīṣa mudrā for the accomplishment of activities.
To expel obstructors and establish the boundary:
this is the heart-seal of the preceding Buddha Family.
Hold the two index fingers upright with their tips touching.
Bend the upper joint into the shape of a hook.
Reciting the mantra, place the seal upon the crown of the head and rotate it three times to the left,
thereby expelling all inauspiciousness and those who create obstacles.
Then, circumambulate three times to the right.
The mantra for accomplishing the boundary (*sīmābandha*) is as follows:
*Namaḥ samantabuddhānām | oṃ ṭaru oṃ maṇḍa svāhā*. Next, perform the Great Samaya-mudrā, which is identical to the aforementioned Armor-mudrā.
The lids are slightly opened in the shape of pestles.
To each of the two wheels, two lids are attached. For the first text below, the mantra is as follows:
Oṃ śaṅkari (pronounced with the tongue rolled back) mahāsamayane svāhā. Recite this mantra accordingly.
Using the seal as before, rotate it three times to the right;
according to the practitioner's intention regarding distance,
bind it as a great boundary (mahā-sīmā).
Next, form the mudrā of the Mother of the Family, Buddhalocanā:
join the two hands in *añjali* and place the two thumbs over the backs of the two index fingers,
shaping them like an eye.
The mantra for joining the two wheels (hands) with the palms is:
*Namaḥ samantabuddhānām | oṃ ru ru sapharu jvala tiṣṭha siddhalocane svāhā*. Next, form the seal of the Tathāgata Uṣṇīṣacakravartin.
This is the same as the previous Buddha-uṣṇīṣa mudrā for accomplishing activities:
join the two wheels (thumbs) together and stand them upright;
bend the two covers (index fingers) flat at their second joints so that their tips touch one another.
Upon the two wheels of the armor,
form the mudrā at the heart and recite the mantra seven times or one hundred and eight times.
Furthermore, empower the five locations of the body once each.
By the power of empowerment (*adhiṣṭhāna*),
one’s body merges with that of the deity into a single essence.
The *Ekākṣara-koṭirāja-dhāraṇī* states:

*Namo samantabuddhānām* | *Bhruṃ* (the syllable *bhruṃ* is pronounced with a rolled tongue as a single sound, drawn out from the chest and throat with a resonance like the beating of a great drum; the earlier translation "Bulin" is an erroneous abbreviation). Next, perform the mudrā for offering the *argha* perfumed water.
This is the aforementioned Great Samaya-mudrā; however,
the two *cchatras* are attached to the backs of the two rays,
and the two wheels are placed at the lower sides of the first *vyañjana*.
Visualize the mudrā as being shaped like a conch shell or a shallow cup,
filled with fragrant water; raise the mudrā so that it is level with the forehead.
Offer scented water.
The mantra for bathing the principal deity and the assembly of noble ones is as follows:
*Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ | oṃ akṣara-ha-akka-varya-praticchana-mañju-svāhā*. Next, form the general mudrā of offering.
With both hands joined hollowly in *añjali*,
cross the upper joints of the five fingers of each hand.
Visualize that from this mudrā, immeasurable incense, flowers, food, drink, palaces, and garments flow forth.
The mantra for making offerings to the assembly of noble ones is as follows:
*Namaḥ sarvabuddhabodhisattvebhyaḥ | oṃ sarvatrāsasaṃkucita-vijvara-śānti namo'stu te svāhā* | Next, form the general Buddha-uṣṇīṣa mudrā.
Then, for the seal of universal offering (*samantapūjā-mudrā*), slightly deepen the interlocking of the fingers so that they reach the middle joints,
like a flower held within the palms.
If the practitioner is pressed by urgent circumstances, [they may proceed thus].
If one is unable to universally bind the seals of the ten Buddha-uṣṇīṣas,
it is sufficient to bind this seal and recite the mantras of the various Buddha-uṣṇīṣas;
this is universally applicable.
For the practitioner as well, there is no error.
The true words are as follows: *Namaḥ samantabuddhānām* (1) *abhisaṃpratiṣṭhitasanānām* (2) *oṃ cakrīṭa oṃ hūṃ* (3). Recite this three times as a hymn of praise.

*Pūrṇa-ni-niṅ-ding-qiè (pūrṇaniṅ) yǐn; shì-nǐ-ní-zhěng-fǎn (śrīṇiñca) yǐn; sà-wǒ-jié-bái-lǎ-fǎn (sarvajvala) yán-jié-fǎn (jvālā); dì-dài-yǐn (dhyāna) shì-nǐ-yī-zhuó-yán-jie-qiè (śrīyayana) shě-sā-wěi-èr-hé (śāmbu) zhuǎn-shé-lǎ-bù-èr-hé (trambuva) nǜ-bì-xīng (ṇika); mǎn-yǐn-dá-wei-fū-bì-fǎn (mandavai) èr-sān-qù-mǎ-bì-sā-duō-èr-hé (smaśānta) wěi-nǐ-yǎ-èr-hé-yǐn (vaineya) dì-pǎ-zuò-gē-luó-èr-hé (dhyānakrama) mǎ-bì-lǐ-níng (mabharīṇi); nǎn-mú-sā-dǔ-èr-hé (namo staute) dì-tā-lǎ-èr-hé (tātra) zuò-gē-luó-èr-hé (krama) lǚ-zhuǎn-shé-dǐ-dǐng-yǐ-fǎn-níng (ḍhiṇi). Fourth: before each recitation, first [recite this].*
By means of the five branches, or by means of the wisdom of contemplation through the five signs, the eight signs, and so forth, one accomplishes the yoga of the principal deity.
These methods are all contained within the *Uṣṇīṣacakravarti-yoga*, which is extremely profound and secret; each must be received personally from a consecrated *ācārya* or [attained] within oneself.

Visualize a single syllable placed in three locations—the crown of the head, the tongue, and the heart—and through the power of that syllable, one is able to become the Honored One, the Cakravartin King of the Crown.
Furthermore, visualize within the maṇḍala a great ocean of fragrant water.
In the center of the ocean is Mount Sumeru,
surrounded on all sides by seven ranges of golden mountains.
Atop the summit of Mount Sumeru is a white eight-petaled lotus flower.
Upon each and every leaf,
the seven treasures of a wheel-turning monarch are arranged in a clockwise sequence:
namely, the golden wheel, the elephant, the horse, the jewel, the woman, the military retinue, and the treasury master.
On the current eighth leaf,
visualize the Honored One Buddhacakṣus,
surrounded before and behind by the retinue of the ten Uṣṇīṣas.
Having first established oneself in this visualization,
one should then perform the recitation while holding the rosary in accordance with the practice,
whether a hundred, a thousand, or up to ten thousand times.
When the constant limit of practice is completed,
hold the *maṇi* jewel at the crown of your head and recite the mantra of the Mother of the Family (*kulamātṛ*).
May the Honored One protect all your meritorious deeds.
Furthermore, bind the root mudrā and apply it to the five places of the body.
Again, bind the universal offering mudrā and perform offerings as before.
Then, gladden the deity with songs of praise.
May your immeasurable compassionate vows protect and sustain us,
enabling us to attain the siddhi of liberation;
may you extensively make great aspirations for the benefit and happiness of sentient beings, vowing to achieve perfect buddhahood.
Next, hold up the argha water and offer it as before.
Then, form the Buddha-uṣṇīṣa-karmakara-mudrā and,
turning to the left, dissolve the boundary.
Furthermore, form the previously described mudrā for welcoming and invitation;
extend the two middle fingers outward and recite the preceding mantra, omitting the syllable *karasaya*.
One should say *visarjaya*,
which constitutes the dismissal.
Furthermore, one should bind the armor mudrā and recite the aforementioned mantra over the five places of the body.
Furthermore, bind the heart-seals (*hṛdaya-mudrā*) of the three families,
prostrate with sincere devotion, and make aspirations;
then, as you please, exit the maṇḍala or perform circumambulation and walking meditation.
Recite Mahāyāna sūtras and perform various virtuous deeds to assist in the accomplishment [of the practice].
*The Essential Method for Recitation of the Buddha-uṣṇīṣa of the Golden-Wheel King*.
